simple: the score you promise to reach, written down before you start.
analogy: the aim on the signed scorecard, written before the first burner is lit.
precise: for one kernel, size and precision, the percentage X of the reference library's speed (reference median time divided by your median time, times 100) that a milestone must reach on your GPU; written in the plan before coding and never lowered afterwards without the owner's explicit approval and a log entry.
source: C1 of MP3 (Systems Curriculum 13.4); D1 of MP3 (Authoring Guide 11.6, MP3 card) — local project documents

simple: a short code computed from the targets file; change one character of a target and the code changes.
analogy: the code written under the scorecard.
precise: in MP3, a 64-bit hash over the lines of the targets file that define the agreement (machine, references, targets, tolerances; not comments or signatures), printed at R1 by the targets check and on every report; equal fingerprints show the report used the signed targets. It detects change, does not prevent it, and is not a cryptographic signature.
source: R4 and R7 of MP3 (runs of targets_lock and mp3_report in this build); hash constants from memory — unverified

simple: the list of matrix sizes the tests use, each chosen to catch one kind of mistake.
analogy: tasting a tiny portion, an odd-sized one and a long thin one, not only the usual platter.
precise: the set of (M, N, K) every correctness test runs: tiny sizes, sizes one below and one above a tile, tall-skinny and short-wide shapes, K = 1, tile multiples and the target sizes; each row is kept with the bug class it targets.
source: C1 of MP3 (Systems Curriculum 13.4 and E6); R1 and R2 of MP3 (suite runs in this build)

simple: the evidence-based answer to why your kernel is slower than the library.
analogy: watching both stations work and noting exactly where your cooks wait.
precise: for each kernel that falls short of its reference, the limiting resource (memory throughput, issue stalls, occupancy, instruction mix) shown by profiler metrics of both kernels, the register and shared-memory report and, where useful, the SASS, ending in a predicted, made and measured change.
source: C1 of MP3 (Systems Curriculum 13.4, E10); D4 of MP3 (Nsight documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program that refuses to print a percentage the measurement rules do not allow.
analogy: the judge who will not score a tasting done with a different clock.
precise: in MP3, the rule set of the report tool: a row is INVALID when the machine differs from the one agreed at R1, the case has no passing correctness check, either side was not timed with device events, no warm-up was recorded, or fewer than 20 timed runs exist.
source: C1 of MP3 (Systems Curriculum 13.4); R5 and R7 of MP3 (runs of mp3_report in this build)

precise: the minimum of N timed runs; more favourable than the median whenever runs vary, so it may be shown next to the median but never used for a verdict under a median-of-at-least-20 protocol.
source: C1 of MP3 (Systems Curriculum 13.4); R5 of MP3

simple: made-up numbers used only to test a program that reads real numbers.
analogy: plastic food used to rehearse the serving.
precise: input files generated by a stated, seeded program and labelled as invented wherever they appear (in MP3 the machine name SYNTHETIC-TEST-DATA); they describe no real machine and support no performance claim.
source: R11 of MP3 (synthetic_raw.py, regenerated byte for byte in this build)
